cards.text: Israel's dividing up the land of Canaan (Joshua 14:1), and now we get the allotment for the clans of the tribe of Judah. The south runs from the Salt Sea past Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Egypt, the east is the Salt Sea, the north climbs right past the Jebusites at Jerusalem, and the west is the Great Sea. That border takes more turns than I did feeling my way around the back of a junk drawer in the dark.

Then Joshua, Israel's leader after Moses (Joshua 1:1-2), gives a portion among the sons of Judah to Caleb son of Jephunneh, one of the spies Moses sent into Canaan (Numbers 13:6). And this is no 'my cousin knows a guy' deal, because Joshua does it according to the LORD's command.

cards.question: Which city does Joshua give to Caleb?

cards.text: Hebron's other name is Kiriath-arba, and Arba was the forefather of Anak. So Caleb gets a city with the other family's name still on the MAILBOX.

cards.question: Caleb's new city of Hebron has descendants of Anak in it. What does Caleb do about them?

cards.text: Caleb just drove out three sons of Anak, and does he take a nap? NO, he marches against Debir, once called Kiriath-sepher, and makes an offer to whoever captures it.

cards.question: Caleb says the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it will get his ___ in marriage.
True or false: Someone takes Caleb up on his offer and captures Kiriath-sepher.

cards.text: So Othniel, son of Caleb's brother Kenaz, takes the city and marries Caleb's daughter Acsah. One day Acsah urges Othniel to ask her father for a field, the oldest married move there is: 'Honey, YOU ask him.'

cards.question: When Acsah gets off her donkey, Caleb has a question for her. What does he ask?
Acsah tells Caleb he has given her land in the Negev. What does she ask him to give her as well?
How does Caleb answer his daughter Acsah's request?

answers.text: He gives her the upper and lower springs
He gives her a field beside Hebron
He sends her back to ask Joshua

cards.text: Then comes Judah's inheritance city by city, each with its villages, from the Negev and the foothills to the hill country and the wilderness, with Beersheba, Lachish, Hebron and En-gedi on the list. First time I read it out loud, I lost my place twice and had to start all over at Kabzeel.
Remember Judah's northern border running right past the Jebusites at Jerusalem? The last verse tells us how Judah does with them.

cards.question: True or false: The descendants of Judah drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem.
So how do things stand in Jerusalem "to this day"?

answers.text: The city lies empty and in ruins
